aspects.fertilizer:
General Linseed Management:
Determine the fertilizer quantity per acre based on laboratory soil analysis.
Balanced fertilizer use is essential to obtain better yield and protect the crop from harmful climate change impacts.
Apply boron to improve flowering and pollination.
If seeds are from private companies, apply fertilizers according to their recommended rates.
For more information, contact the nearest government soil and water testing laboratory.

Average Fertility Soil:
Use 23 kilograms nitrogen, 23 kilograms phosphorus, and 12 kilograms potash per acre.
Apply 1 bag of DAP, two-thirds of a bag of urea, and half a bag of SOP or MOP per acre.
Alternatively, apply 1 bag of TSP, 1 bag of urea, and half a bag of SOP or MOP per acre.
If ammonium sulfate is available, use it instead of urea.
If SOP is not available, MOP can be used, but apply sulfur at 2 kilograms per acre with it.

Rain-fed Areas:
Apply the entire quantity of fertilizer at the time of sowing.

Irrigated Areas:
Apply the full dose of phosphorus and potash fertilizers, along with one-third of the nitrogen fertilizer, at sowing time.
Apply the remaining nitrogen fertilizer in two installments.
Apply half of the remaining nitrogen with the first irrigation.
Apply the other half of the remaining nitrogen before flowering.
Apply 4 to 5 kilograms of sulfur per acre with the second irrigation to improve yield and quality.

Punjab Technology:
The Soil Fertility Research Institute Punjab Lahore developed a free mobile app named Khad Hisab.
Farmers can download it for free from the Google Play Store.
The app provides recommended fertilizer amounts for linseed and other crops, both with or without a soil test report.
Farmers can calculate balanced fertilizers according to their resources to increase yield and profit.
Watch the short introductory video in the app to learn how to use it.
aspects.harvesting:
Harvesting:
Linseed sown at the recommended time matures in late April or early May.
Harvest the crop on time.

Spraying and Chemical Safety:
Use a flat fan or flood jet nozzle for weed control.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect pest control.
Bury empty poison bottles in the ground.
Dispose of cardboard boxes.

Storage:
Ensure linseed is thoroughly dried before storage.
Moisture content must not exceed 8 percent.
The seed must make a cracking sound when chewed with teeth.
High moisture causes a risk of fungal attack on the seed.
Do not mix different varieties during seed storage.
Inspect warehouses regularly to protect stored linseed from insect attack.
Fumigate stores using 30 to 35 tablets of aluminium phosphide per 1000 cubic feet to prevent insect attack.

Domestic Oil Refining:
Extract oil using a kohlu or expeller.
Refining linseed oil at the domestic level makes it relatively cheap, free from impurities, nutritious, and usable as an excellent cooking oil.
Place 5 kilograms of raw linseed oil into a pot or pan and heat it to 85 degrees Celsius.
Do not allow the oil to boil, but heat it so the pot cannot be touched by hand.
Add 150 grams of finely ground gachni or fuller's earth to the hot oil.
Stir thoroughly with a spoon for 5 minutes, then remove it from the stove.
Make a triangular bag from thick market cloth.
Hang the bag from a sturdy stand or charpai and place a clean container underneath.
Pour the lukewarm oil into the bag to filter it.

Farmer Guidance:
The Directorate General of Agriculture Information conducts a publicity campaign through print, electronic, and social media to guide farmers from sowing to harvesting.
aspects.irrigation:
Rain-fed areas:
Summer rains are very important for Rabi crops including linseed.
Linseed is cultivated using moisture conserved from summer rains.
Methods should be adopted so summer rainwater absorbs into the soil and remains conserved rather than wasting as runoff.
Conserving monsoon rainwater well can increase Rabi crop yields by 20 to 25 percent.

Irrigation schedule:
Apply 3 to 4 irrigations to the linseed crop.
Give the first irrigation before flowering.
Give the second irrigation after flowering.
Give the third irrigation at capsule formation.
Take special care of irrigation in case of drought.

Excessive rain management:
Sow the crop on ridges to protect it from the effects of heavy rains.
Sowing on ridges minimizes crop damage and makes it easy to drain excess water from the field.

General management:
Sow the crop at the recommended time for better care.
Take special care of plant protection.
Stay updated on weather forecasts before sowing and when applying irrigation.
aspects.machinery:
Ridge sowing machinery:
Broadcast seed and fertilizer after land preparation. Run a plow and plank. Make ridges at a distance of 2.5 feet using a tractor. A planter called a ridger-cum-seeder has been introduced by various companies and is available in the market for this method of cultivation.

Spraying procedure:
Before spraying the linseed crop, check the machine with plain water to determine the required water volume. Do not spray during strong winds. Do not stand against the wind direction while spraying. Use the recommended volume of water to ensure uniform spray coverage. Avoid repeated applications of pesticides from the same group.

Nozzle types:
Use a flat fan nozzle or a flood jet nozzle for weed control. Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect pest control.

Pesticide waste disposal:
Bury empty pesticide bottles in the ground. Dispose of cardboard boxes.
aspects.other:
**Greens harvesting:**
Plucking greens from the linseed crop increases the risk of aphid attack.
Plucking greens reduces linseed crop yield.
Farmers should allocate a separate land area for harvesting greens to protect the seed crop from damage.

**Industrial and commercial uses:**
Oilseeds Research Institute Faisalabad and National Textile University Faisalabad collaborated on linseed.
Linseed seeds are used for oil and medicinal purposes.
National Textile University processes linseed straw into fiber for the textile industry.
The textile industry manufactures good quality denim from linseed fiber and exports it for better market rates.
Linseed products and seeds are exported to earn foreign exchange for the national economy and increase farmer profits.

**Climate change management:**
Unexpected heavy rains and drought caused by climate change harm the linseed crop.
Sow the crop at the recommended time to protect it from climate change effects.
Implement proper plant protection measures.
Check the weather forecast before sowing or applying irrigation water.

**High rainfall areas:**
Linseed must be cultivated on ridges in high rainfall areas.

**Farmer training:**
Linseed training programs are held at the district and tehsil levels.
Agricultural experts train Agriculture Extension staff and farmers on modern production technologies.
aspects.overview:
General Overview:
Linseed is a Rabi oilseed crop. 
Linseed seed contains 39 to 44 percent oil. 
The oil dries quickly and is used for varnish, paint, printing ink, high-quality soap, and fine colors. 
Stem fiber is used to make high-quality linen fabric. 
Linseed is consumed as food, including traditional winter sweet pinniyan. 
Linseed oil cake is used as animal feed. 
The 2025-26 oilseed production plan includes linseed, canola, mustard, raya, taramira, and camelina to increase domestic edible oil production and reduce imports.

Barani Areas:
Linseed is sown using soil moisture conserved from summer monsoon rains. 
Conserving summer rainwater increases Rabi crop yields by 20 to 25 percent.

Varieties:
Roshni was developed by Oilseeds Research Institute Faisalabad and approved in 2018. 
Roshni resists diseases, insect pests, and lodging. 
Roshni yield potential is 18 to 22 maunds per acre. 
Chandni resists lodging, pests, and diseases. 
Chandni seed contains 40 to 42 percent oil. 
Chandni yield potential is 15 to 20 maunds per acre.

Punjab Statistics (First Series):
In 2020-21, linseed area was 413.50 thousand acres (167.34 thousand hectares), production was 267.26 thousand metric tons, and yield was 16.16 maunds per acre. 
In 2021-22, area was 585.50 thousand acres (236.94 thousand hectares), production was 403.00 thousand metric tons, and yield was 17.21 maunds per acre. 
In 2022-23, area was 1055.10 thousand acres (426.98 thousand hectares), production was 665.71 thousand metric tons, and yield was 15.77 maunds per acre. 
In 2023-24, area was 605.20 thousand acres (244.91 thousand hectares), production was 314.47 thousand metric tons, and yield was 12.99 maunds per acre. 
In 2024-25 provisional estimates, area was 820.65 thousand acres (332.10 thousand hectares), production was 499.94 thousand metric tons, and yield was 15.23 maunds per acre.

Punjab Statistics (Second Series):
In 2019-20, linseed area was 733 acres (297 hectares), production was 210 metric tons, and yield was 7.16 maunds per acre (708 kg per hectare). 
In 2020-21, area was 979 acres (396 hectares), production was 298 metric tons, and yield was 7.61 maunds per acre (752 kg per hectare). 
In 2021-22, area was 752 acres (304 hectares), production was 211 metric tons, and yield was 7.01 maunds per acre (693 kg per hectare). 
In 2022-23, area was 2034 acres (823 hectares), production was 689 metric tons, and yield was 8.46 maunds per acre (836 kg per hectare). 
In 2023-24, area was 2022 acres (818 hectares), production was 570 metric tons, and yield was 7.04 maunds per acre (697 kg per hectare).

Extension and Outreach:
Extension staff writes recommendations on walls, markers, and signboards. 
The Deputy Director of Agriculture Extension sets district targets and informs the provincial government. 
The Directorate General of Agricultural Information runs campaigns across print, electronic, and social media from sowing to harvest.
aspects.pests_diseases:
General Crop Protection:
Linseed has strong natural resistance against diseases, insects, and shattering. Treat seed before sowing with recommended fungicide at 1 gram per kilogram seed. Do not increase chemical dose and maintain appropriate water volume to prevent poor germination; do not apply if precautions cannot be maintained. Avoid early sowing. Practice crop rotation, remove weeds, use healthy seed, and destroy crop residues.

Storage:
Fumigate stored linseed with 30 to 35 tablets of Aluminium Phosphide per 1000 cubic feet against storage insects.

Termites:
Pale yellow insects attack underground parts during dry weather, causing plants to dry and pull out easily. Apply 1 liter Fipronil 5 percent SC per acre flooded with water during rauni in empty fields or upon crop attack.
Rain-fed Areas:
Mix recommended termite pesticide into 15 to 20 kilograms fine soil, broadcast before sowing, and plough.

Toka:
Pest attacks emerging seedlings, primarily near sugarcane, maize, and sorghum. Spray 330 milliliters Lambda Cyhalothrin 2.5 EC or 250 milliliters Bifenthrin 10 EC per acre.

Sawfly:
Wrinkled dark greenish-black larvae with five black stripes attack in October and November, leaving leaf veins. Spray per acre 80 milliliters Spinetoram 120 SC, 330 milliliters Lambda Cyhalothrin 2.5 percent EC, 200 milliliters Emamectin Benzoate 1.9 EC, or 30 grams Fipronil 80 WG.

Spotted Bug:
Nymphs and adults suck sap in October and November. Spray per acre 400 milliliters Abamectin plus Thiamethoxam 108 SC, 100 grams Dinotefuran 20 percent SG, 250 grams Acephate 75 SP, or 250 milliliters Bifenthrin 10 EC.

Cabbage Butterfly:
Caterpillars devour leaves in patches. Spray per acre 80 milliliters Chlorantraniliprole plus Thiamethoxam 300 SC, 80 milliliters Spinetoram 120 SC, 50 milliliters Flubendiamide 480 SC, or 250 milliliters Lambda Cyhalothrin 2.5 EC.

Aphids:
Pests attack in clusters from mid-January to late March. Complete sowing in the first week of October to avoid damage. Spray per acre 24 grams Thiamethoxam 25 SWG, 100 grams Dinotefuran 20 percent SG, 60 grams Flonicamid 50 WG, or 200 milliliters Clothianidin 20 EC.
Punjab Biological Control:
Free Chrysoperla cards are provided from eleven Punjab Agriculture Extension biological laboratories in Sahiwal, Faisalabad, Hafizabad, Layyah, Vehari, Pakpattan, Sheikhupura, Jhang, Muzaffargarh, Okara, and Toba Tek Singh.

Diseases and Sprays per Liter Water:
For white rust, spray 1.25 milliliters Propiconazole or Difenoconazole.
For epidemic blight at 10 to 25 degrees Celsius during rains, spray 1 gram Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 2.5 milliliters Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole.
For downy mildew, spray 5 grams Fluomorph plus Fosetyl-aluminium or 6 grams Mancozeb plus Cymoxanil.
For bacterial stem rot during persistent smog, spray 2.5 milliliters Benzothiazolinone, 1 gram Streptomycin sulphate, or 6 milliliters Kasugamycin.
For stem rot, treat seed with 1 gram Thiophanate-methyl per kilogram seed, or spray 2.5 milliliters Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole.
For plant blight, spray 1 gram Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 3.5 grams Metiram plus Pyraclostrobin.
For rust, spray 1 gram Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 2 milliliters Propiconazole.

Application Safety:
Spray during evening hours at economic threshold levels using hollow cone nozzles. Do not hoe immediately after spraying. Wear protective gear and bury empty pesticide containers.
aspects.sowing:
**Sowing Time:**
The best sowing time for linseed is from 15 October to 15 November.

**Seed Rate:**
Use 6 kg of seed per acre in irrigated areas.
Use 8 kg of seed per acre in rain-fed areas.

**Soil and Land Preparation:**
Medium loam soil is preferred.
Plow and plank two to three times for land preparation.
Level the land with a laser leveler for good germination and growth.

**Rain-fed Land Preparation:**
Deep plow empty fields before the rainy season to conserve moisture.
Strengthen field bunds.
Plow as needed, level the land, and plow across the slope.
Do not plow after the rainy season.
Before sowing, plow twice and plank to preserve moisture.
Ensure the field is level and weed-free at sowing time.
Prepare land in the evening or before sunrise to prevent moisture loss.

**Sowing Methods:**
For drill sowing, keep row-to-row spacing at 1 foot.
Ensure seed depth does not exceed 1.5 inches.
For ridge sowing, broadcast seed and fertilizer after preparation, plow and plank, and make ridges 2.5 feet apart using a tractor.
A ridger cum seeder planter is commercially available for ridge sowing.
Ridge sowing protects the crop from excess rain and makes water drainage easier.

**Thinning:**
Thinning must be completed before the first irrigation.
Thin when plants develop four leaves.
Remove weak and diseased plants during thinning.
Maintain a plant spacing of 9 to 12 inches.

**Weed Control:**
For drill or moisture sowing, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre before the final plowing.
For ridge sowing, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre within 24 hours after sowing.

**Irrigation and General Management:**
Check weather forecasts before sowing or watering.
Manage irrigation carefully during drought conditions.
Ensure proper plant protection care.
aspects.varieties:
Seed Sourcing and Certification:
Limited linseed seed is available from Punjab Seed Corporation, National Agricultural Research Centre Islamabad, Linseed Section at Ayub Agricultural Research Institute Faisalabad, Linseed Research Station Khanpur, Regional Agricultural Research Institute Bahawalpur, and Barani Agricultural Research Institute Chakwal. Recommended varieties are also available from registered private seed companies. Farmers should always use seed certified by the Federal Seed Certification Department.

Approved Varieties:
Approved linseed varieties are Roshni and Chandni.
Roshni was developed by the Oilseeds Research Institute Faisalabad and approved in 2018. It resists diseases, pests, and lodging, and yields 18 to 22 maunds per acre.
Chandni resists lodging, pests, and diseases. Its seed contains 40 to 42 percent oil, and it yields 15 to 20 maunds per acre.

Sowing and Seed Rate:
The best sowing time is 15 October to 15 November.
The seed rate for irrigated areas is 6 kg per acre.
The seed rate for rain-fed barani areas is 8 kg per acre.
Prepare the land thoroughly and level it with a laser leveler.
Sowing depth must not exceed 1.5 inches.

General Seed Treatment:
Apply recommended fungicide at 1 gram per kg seed to prevent diseases.
Do not exceed the chemical dose and use appropriate water to avoid damaging germination.
Do not apply fungicide if this precaution cannot be maintained.

Wilt Management:
Wilt causes seed rot, plant drying, and cracked root bark.
Prevent wilt by treating seeds with recommended fungicide, avoiding early sowing, removing weeds, and rotating crops.

Epidemic Blight Management:
Use healthy seed, rotate crops, and destroy crop residues.
When temperatures are between 10 and 25 degrees Celsius during rainfall, spray before symptoms appear.
Spray Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin at 1 gram per liter of water, or Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter of water.

Plant Blight Management:
Grow resistant varieties, rotate crops, and plant seed treated with recommended fungicide.
When symptoms appear, spray Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin at 1 gram per liter of water, or Metiram plus Pyraclostrobin at 3.5 grams per liter of water.

Downy Mildew Management:
Use healthy seed and destroy crop residues.
When symptoms appear, spray Flumorph plus Fosetyl-aluminium at 5 grams per liter of water, or Mancozeb plus Cymoxanil at 6 grams per liter of water.

Stem Rot Management:
Treat seed at sowing with Thiophanate-methyl at 1 gram per kg seed.
If disease appears on the crop, spray Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter of water.
aspects.weeds:
**Rain-fed areas:**
Deep plough empty fields before the monsoon to preserve rainwater moisture.
Strengthen field bunds, level the land, and plough across the slope.
Do not plough after the monsoon season.
Before sowing, plough twice and apply planking to prevent moisture loss.
Prepare land in the evening or before sunrise to keep moisture from drying out.
Ensure fields are level and weed-free at sowing time.

**Common weeds:**
Common weeds in linseed are Jai, Dumbi Sitti, Lashkani booti, Bathu, Karund, Shahtra, and It-sit.

**Non-chemical weed control:**
Use the dab method after soaking irrigation or rain when soil is at workable moisture.
For the dab method, plough, apply heavy planking, and leave the field undisturbed for 5 to 7 days.
Weeds will germinate and get destroyed during final seedbed preparation.
Perform dry hoeing after crop emergence, preferably before rainfall.
Do the first hoeing before the first irrigation.
Do the second hoeing after irrigation when the soil reaches workable moisture condition.
Thin the crop when plants reach four leaves to maintain recommended spacing.

**Chemical weed control:**
Apply pre-emergence Pendimethalin at 1000 ml per acre.
In moderate weather with temperatures at 35 degrees Celsius or below, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre mixed in 100 liters of water immediately after sowing.
For drill and moisture sowing methods, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre before the final ploughing.
For ridge sowing, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre within 24 hours after sowing.
To control emerged It-sit within two weeks after crop emergence, spray Betazachlor 50 percent SC at 400 to 500 ml per acre.
This Betazachlor spray can be done without a shield.

**Equipment and safety:**
Use a flat fan or flood jet nozzle for weed control sprays.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect pest sprays.
Never hoe the field immediately after spraying herbicide.
Hoeing immediately breaks the chemical barrier, allows weeds to regrow, and exposes farmers to inhaled chemical dust.
Bury empty chemical bottles underground and destroy cardboard packaging.

**Disease and weed management:**
Linseed wilt causes rotting seeds, plant wilting, drying, and cracked root bark.
Prevent wilt by treating seeds with recommended fungicide, avoiding early sowing, destroying weeds, and rotating crops.
